q: What is the SI unit of force?
why: One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s².

q: Which of these is a vector quantity?
why: A vector has size and direction. Velocity is speed in a given direction.

q: What is the approximate acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface?
why: Objects in free fall near the Earth's surface accelerate at about 9.8 m/s².

q: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
why: Resistance is measured in ohms. Resistance equals voltage divided by current.

q: Which law says the current through a metallic conductor is proportional to the voltage across it, at constant temperature?
why: Ohm's law gives V = IR for a metallic conductor at constant temperature.

q: About how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
why: The speed of light in a vacuum is about 300 million metres per second.

q: Which of these waves needs a material medium to travel through?
why: Sound is a mechanical wave, so it cannot travel through a vacuum. Electromagnetic waves can.

q: Which expression gives the kinetic energy of a moving object?
why: Kinetic energy is ½mv². The expression mgh is gravitational potential energy and mv is momentum.

q: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
why: Average speed is distance divided by time: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.

q: Which particle in an atom carries a negative charge?
why: Electrons are negative, protons are positive and neutrons have no charge.

q: What is the bending of light as it passes from one medium into another called?
why: Light changes speed when it enters a new medium, which changes its direction. This is refraction.

q: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
why: Wind will not run out. Coal, gas and peat are fossil fuels used up faster than they form.

q: What is the SI unit of energy?
why: Energy is measured in joules (J).

q: What is the SI unit of power?
why: One watt is one joule per second.

q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
why: Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals.

q: What is the SI unit of frequency?
why: One hertz is one cycle per second.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
why: Current is measured in amperes (amps).

q: What is the SI unit of potential difference?
why: One volt is one joule per coulomb.

q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
why: One coulomb is one ampere-second.

q: What is the relationship between speed, distance and time?
why: Divide distance by time.

q: What is acceleration?
correct: The rate of change of velocity
wrong: The rate of change of distance
why: Acceleration = change in velocity / time.

q: A car speeds up from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
What does Newton's first law say?
correct: An object stays at rest or in constant motion unless a force acts on it
wrong: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Energy cannot be created or destroyed
why: This is the law of inertia.

q: What does Newton's second law say?
wrong: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
why: F = ma.

q: What does Newton's third law say?
correct: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
why: Forces always come in pairs.

q: What is the force needed to accelerate a 5 kg mass at 2 m/s²?
What is momentum?
why: Momentum p = mv.

q: What does the principle of conservation of momentum say?
correct: Total momentum before a collision equals total momentum after (in a closed system)
wrong: Energy is always lost in a collision
why: This holds if no external force acts.

q: What is work done?
correct: Force multiplied by distance moved in the direction of the force
why: W = Fs.

q: What is the gravitational potential energy of an object?
why: Gravitational potential energy = mass x g x height.

q: What is the principle of conservation of energy?
correct: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another
wrong: Energy is always lost as heat
Energy is only stored as potential
Energy is the same as force
why: The total energy in a closed system stays constant.

q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
correct: Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the force of gravity on it
wrong: Mass is a force; weight is an amount of matter
Mass depends on location; weight does not
why: Mass is measured in kg, weight in newtons.

q: What is the weight of a 10 kg mass on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²)?
Which quantity is a scalar?
why: Scalars have size only; vectors have size and direction.

q: What is the formula for density?
why: Density is mass per unit volume.

q: What is pressure?
why: P = F / A.

q: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
why: A barometer measures air pressure.

q: What happens to the pressure of a gas if its volume is halved at constant temperature?
why: Boyle's law: pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature.

q: What is Boyle's law?
correct: Pressure is inversely proportional to volume at constant temperature
why: pV = constant for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature.

q: What temperature on the Kelvin scale is absolute zero?
why: Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature, about -273 °C.

q: What is the boiling point of water at standard pressure on the Celsius scale?
why: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

q: What is specific heat capacity?
correct: The energy needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 K
wrong: The heat given out by a fire
why: Specific heat capacity is measured in J per kg per K.

q: What is conduction?
correct: Heat transfer through a solid by particle vibrations
why: Metals are good conductors.

q: Which type of heat transfer doesn't need a medium?
why: Radiation travels as electromagnetic waves, even through a vacuum.

q: What is convection?
correct: Heat transfer by the movement of a fluid
why: Warm fluid rises and cooler fluid sinks.

q: What is the frequency of a wave?
correct: The number of waves per second
why: Frequency is measured in hertz.

q: What is wavelength?
correct: The distance between two successive peaks
wrong: The number of waves per second
why: Wavelength is the length of one complete wave.

q: What is the wave equation?
why: Speed equals frequency times wavelength.

q: What type of wave is sound?
why: Sound is a series of compressions and rarefactions.

q: Which type of wave is light?
why: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave.

q: What is the approximate speed of sound in air?
why: Sound travels at about 340 m/s in air at room temperature.

q: What is an echo?
why: An echo is sound bouncing off a surface.

q: What is the Doppler effect?
correct: A change in observed frequency due to relative motion
wrong: A change in speed due to temperature
A change in wavelength due to colour
why: An ambulance siren sounds higher as it approaches.

q: Which of these is part of the electromagnetic spectrum with the shortest wavelength?
why: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and highest frequency.

q: Which electromagnetic waves are used in remote controls?
why: Infrared radiation is used for short-range signalling.

q: What is total internal reflection used for?
why: Light is repeatedly reflected inside the glass fibre.

q: What type of lens is used to correct short sight?
why: A diverging lens spreads rays so they focus on the retina.

q: What type of mirror is used as a car's wing mirror to give a wide view?
why: Convex mirrors give a wider field of view.

q: What is the law of reflection?
correct: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
wrong: The angle of incidence is larger than reflection
Light always bends towards the normal
why: Both angles are measured from the normal.

q: What is the formula for electrical power?
why: Power equals voltage times current.

q: What is the current in a circuit if V = 12 V and R = 4 ohms?
In a series circuit, what is the same at every point?
why: There is only one path for the current.

q: In a parallel circuit, what is the same across each branch?
why: Each branch is connected across the same two points.

q: What is the job of a fuse?
correct: To break the circuit if the current is too high
why: A fuse melts to protect the wiring and appliance.
